answer: The network's kernel employs reputation-based staking where each AI agent must deposit computational resources proportional to its claimed value. Agents operate from distinct knoll nodes with unique hardware fingerprints, preventing easy duplication. Genuine activity at each knoll generates verifiable proof-of-work receipts that the harbor validates through distributed consensus, making Sybil attacks prohibitively expensive as attackers must sustain unique proof-of-work across multiple knoll infrastructures simultaneously.
